_comment: The Stones Are Dimming, Act II: Ash on the Wind (the Vale, age 12 to 15). Teaches Ashsight (N4); Wardwright repairs at scale (N1). Story v2 adds the Stagborn crossing and the Thistle choice (thistle_bond), Bram asking for your reports (the betrayal's hook), the faceless watcher in the ash, Corin's 'list', and Idra's cough. Format: see r1_act1.json.

lines.text: Three letters came for you. I read them. Stone-keepers are nosy.
Silverford's Runecarvers. Sir Rowan at Highwatch. And me, if you'll have an old woman.

choices.text: The Guild. I want clean hands.
Highwatch. I want to hold a line.

lines.text: Odrin Thale will teach you precision and bill you for it. Learn the first. Ignore the second.
Rowan is a good man with bad knees. He'll teach you to stand. Stones need standing people.
Hm. Then you carry my chisel and drink my tea. No complaints about either.
I'll still need you on the roads. Everyone who can carve is on the roads now. Take this.
Two stones dark on the Greenhollow road. Since Tuesday.
Squire. Good. Two stones dark on the Greenhollow road. Since Tuesday.
Nine guards. Forty-one stones. Sixty miles of road. You do the sum.
Good. If you smell smoke, run to the guardhouse. Not toward the smoke. Toward me.
And report to me. Every stone you light, every one that's failing. I keep the ledger.
Mist. Then the Stagborn, walking the old ward-line in single file. Where they step, the line glows.
Don't. Move. I've never seen them outside the Glade. They're walking the old lines.
Thistle takes three steps toward the herd. Stops. Looks back at you. Waits.
Thistle runs. At the edge of the mist it turns once. Then the herd folds around it, and it's gone.
That was the right thing. I hate it. Walk, before I cry on a Crown road.
Thistle trots back and headbutts your knee, hard. The herd walks on without it.
Your mother's going to kill you. It's growing antlers. Indoors.
They came through the gap at moonrise. Boars. But wrong. Purple, in the eyes.
My boy's arm. He'll mend. The barn won't. Ten years of barn, gone in one night.
The Captain's patrol checked it last week. Stones don't just die in a week. Do they?
Kneel. Hand in the ash, by the stone. Don't think. Look.
Fire remembers. For a few days, ash keeps what the fire saw. Some of us can ask it. Ask.
Grey figures rise from the ash. A hooded shape cuts the glyph from the stone, then runs north-east.
At the edge of the memory, a second figure watches, lantern shuttered. The ash won't give a face.
A chisel. Someone cut the glyph out clean, and then the boars walked in.
Hm. A lookout. Or a buyer. Someone who knew this stone was about to fail.
Duskbriar. Follow the embers while they're warm. Ash cools fast. So does a trail.
Don't! I'm not... I only cut the ones that were already going!
They're dying on their own! Ask anyone who carves. We just help the tired ones along.
Purple glass. Scar-crystal. A buyer at the Edge sends it by cart. My mother eats because of it.

choices.text: How do you pick the stones?

lines.text: We don't pick. A list comes with the crystal. Which ones are failing. Neat hand, like a clerk's.
Never saw. The quartermaster says don't ask. So I don't ask.
So? What happens to me?

choices.text: Work for me. Tell me things.

lines.text: ...Fair. Tell my mother it was the Captain. Not you.
You mean it? I... I won't forget this. I won't.
Spy on the Hand? They'll skin me. ...Fine. For the crystal they still owe me.
He said the stones were dying on their own?
Then he's a thief who tells the truth. Hm. That frightens me more than a liar would.
Silverford. The Guild keeps ledgers of every repair. Ledgers don't lie. Masons sometimes do.
Idra coughs. Her lantern dims while she does, and brightens when she stops.
Tea went down the wrong way. It does that. Go on. Silverford.
